newsitem.title: USA: Texaco employees remain in settlement.
newsitem.headline: Texaco employees remain in settlement.

text.p: Texaco Inc.'s agreement to settle a racial discrimination suit for $176.1 million has passed another hurdle on the road to final approval with no potential claimants asking to opt out of the accord, a plaintiff's lawyer said Wednesday.
The proposed settlement, which was reached in November, still requires court approval and a fairness hearing on the accord is set for March 18.
The federal class action suit, which was filed in 1994, alleged that Texaco systematically discriminated against minority employees in promotions and had fostered a racially hostile environment.

Steven Singer of Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossman, one of the law firms representing the plaintiffs, said that more than 1,300 notices had been sent to potential class members but none had elected to opt out of the settlement as of Tuesday's deadline.
"This speaks to how good the settlement is," Singer said.
If a substantial number of potential claimants had decided to opt out, Texaco could have withdrawn its agreement.
In January, Texaco and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission reached an agreement that would allow the commission to intervene in the suit.

Under the agreement reached with Texaco, the commission can monitor the company's compliance with federal law by inspecting its premises and records as well as interviewing current or former employees.
